#Prepare the model and define variables
```{r}
#The outcome vector X:
X_biomark <- t(counts_batch_corrected_combined) #MINT expects samples as rows and genes as columns, so the data must be transposed
X_biomark <- as.matrix(X_biomark)

#The outcome vector Y:
outcome_biomark <- filtered_meta_combined$status #status is affected or unaffected
outcome_biomark <- factor(outcome_biomark)

#Defining where the data comes from:
study_biomark <- filtered_meta_combined$data #data is RRC or Mote_CIL. 
study_biomark <- factor(study_biomark)

#Experiemental Design
table(outcome_biomark,study_biomark)
```


#Create a basic mint model for tuning
```{r}
basic_mint_biomark <- mint.splsda(X=X, Y=outcome, study=study, ncomp = 2)

basic_mint__biomark_perf <- perf(basic_mint_biomark, folds = 2, nrepeat =50)
plot(basic_mint_perf)
```


##Tune the model
```{r}
#grid of possible keepX values. This specifies the number of genes the model will test retaining on each component. Start at 1 gene, end at 100 genes, increase by 1 each time

#mahalanobis.dist
tune_mint_biomark1 <- tune(X=X_biomark, Y=outcome_biomark, study=study_biomark,
                             ncomp=10,
                             validation = 'loo',
                             measure = 'BER',
                             dist = "mahalanobis.dist",
                             test.keepX = seq(1,100,1), #From Natalia? Comment above.
                             method = "mint.splsda")
plot(tune_mint_biomark1, sd=FALSE) #sd = false due to LOO CV


#centroids.dist
tune_mint_biomark2 <- tune(X=X_biomark, Y=outcome_biomark, study=study_biomark,
                             ncomp=10,
                             validation = 'loo',
                             measure = 'BER',
                             dist = "centroids.dist",
                             test.keepX = seq(1,100,1), #From Natalia. Comment above.
                             method = "mint.splsda")
plot(tune_mint_biomark2, sd=FALSE) #sd = false due to LOO CV


#max.dist
tune_mint_biomark3 <- tune(X=X_biomark, Y=outcome_biomark, study=study_biomark,
                             ncomp=10,
                             validation = 'loo',
                             measure = 'BER',
                             dist = "max.dist",
                             test.keepX = seq(1,100,1), #From Natalia. Comment above.
                             method = "mint.splsda")
plot(tune_mint_biomark3, sd=FALSE) #sd = false due to LOO CV
```
The tuning results here are different. I'm keeping them just to see the differences between the full data and the train data. However, I will follow the pipeline previously established. Therefore, the remaining code is based off the max.dist parameter from the previous training model.



##Extract the optimal keepX parameter
```{r}
optimal_ncomp_biomark <- 7

optimal_keepX_biomark <-tune_mint_biomark1$choice.keepX[1:optimal_ncomp_biomark]
optimal_keepX_biomark
```
ncomp is the number of components to include in the model. optimal_keepx is determining the the optimal amount of features for each component


#Train MINT sPLS-DA model
```{r}
#sPLS-DA model
mint_splsda_biomark <- mint.splsda(X=X_biomark, Y=outcome_biomark, study=study_biomark, ncomp=optimal_ncomp, keepX = optimal_keepX)

#Plots
plotIndiv(mint_splsda_biomark, study='global', legend = TRUE,
          title = 'MINT sPLS-DA',
          subtitle = 'Global', ellipse = TRUE)

plotIndiv(mint_splsda_biomark, study='all.partial', legend = TRUE,
          title = 'MINT sPLS-DA',
          subtitle = paste('all.partial', 1:2))
```



##Variable Plots for MINT sPLS-DA with Batch Included
####Correlation Circle plots
```{r}
#Components 1 vs 2
plotVar(mint_splsda_biomark, comp = c(1,2), title = "Correlation Circle Plot: Comp 1 vs Comp 2", cutoff = 0.5)

#Components 1 vs components 3
plotVar(mint_splsda_biomark, comp = c(1,3), title = "Correlation Circle Plot: Comp 1 vs Comp 3", cutoff = 0.5)

#Components 2 vs components 3
plotVar(mint_splsda_biomark, comp = c(2,3), title = "Correlation Circle Plot: Comp 2 vs Comp 3", cutoff = 0.5)

#Components 2 vs components 4
plotVar(mint_splsda_biomark, comp = c(2,4), title = "Correlation Circle Plot: Comp 2 vs Comp 4", cutoff = 0.5)

#Components 2 vs components 7
plotVar(mint_splsda_biomark, comp = c(2,7), title = "Correlation Circle Plot: Comp 2 vs Comp 7", cutoff = 0.5)
```





####Bar Variable Plots
```{r}
#Since I am looking for genes with the same directionality across both studies, I need to look at all.partial variable plots instead of global

comp1<- plotLoadings(mint_splsda_biomark, contrib = "max", method = "mean", comp = 1, legend = T, study = "all.partial", title = "Contribution on comp 1", subtitle = c("Mote_CIL", "RRC"))

comp2<- plotLoadings(mint_splsda_biomark, contrib = "max", method = "mean", comp = 2, legend = T, study = "all.partial", title = "Contribution on comp 2", subtitle = c("Mote_CIL", "RRC"))

comp3<- plotLoadings(mint_splsda_biomark, contrib = "max", method = "mean", comp = 3, legend = T, study = "all.partial", title = "Contribution on comp 3", subtitle = c("Mote_CIL", "RRC"))


comp4<- plotLoadings(mint_splsda_biomark, contrib = "max", method = "mean", comp = 4, legend = T, study = "all.partial", title = "Contribution on comp 4", subtitle = c("Mote_CIL", "RRC"))

comp5<- plotLoadings(mint_splsda_biomark, contrib = "max", method = "mean", comp = 5, legend = T, study = "all.partial", title = "Contribution on comp 5", subtitle = c("Mote_CIL", "RRC"))

comp6<- plotLoadings(mint_splsda_biomark, contrib = "max", method = "mean", comp = 6, legend = T, study = "all.partial", title = "Contribution on comp 6", subtitle = c("Mote_CIL", "RRC"))

comp7<- plotLoadings(mint_splsda_biomark, contrib = "max", method = "mean", comp = 7, legend = T, study = "all.partial", title = "Contribution on comp 7", subtitle = c("Mote_CIL", "RRC"))
```



#Test MINT sPLS-DA model with the tuned data
##Determine which distance metric to use
```{r}
mint_biomark_perf <- perf(mint_splsda_biomark, folds = 3, nrepeat =50)
plot(mint_splsda_perf)
```

#Extract biomarkers
```{r}
mint_genes <- list()
for (i in 1:7) {
  mint_genes[[i]] <- selectVar(mint_splsda_biomark, comp = i)$value
names(mint_genes)[i]<-paste("Component",i)}
print(mint_genes)

print(mint_genes$rrc)
```
